ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Anyone who's had an apple may know that pieces of an apple stick together, when picking up one piece a second piece may also come with the first piece. The same idea is tried on a golden apple. Consider two uniform hemispheres with radius $r=4 \mathrm{~cm}$ made of gold of density $\rho_{g}=19300 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$. The top half is nailed to a support and the space between is filled with water.
<image_1>

Given that the surface tension of water is $\gamma=0.072 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~m}^{-1}$ and that the contact angle between gold and water is $\theta=10^{\circ}$, what is the maximum distance between the two hemispheres so that the bottom half doesn't fall? Answer in millimeters.

Anyone who's had an apple may know that pieces of an apple stick together: when picking up one piece, a second piece may also come with the first piece. The same idea is tried on a golden apple. Consider two uniform hemispheres with radius $r=4\ \mathrm{cm}$ made of gold of density $\rho_g=19300\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. The top half is nailed to a support and the space between them is filled with water.

Given that the surface tension of water is $\gamma=0.072\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}$ and that the contact angle between gold and water is $\theta=10^{\circ}$, what is the maximum distance between the two hemispheres so that the bottom half doesn't fall? Answer in millimeters.

method.method_draft: Use a direct Young-Laplace pressure-balance calculation. Treat the facing flat cuts of the two hemispheres as parallel circular plates of radius r separated by an unknown small gap d filled with water. The meniscus at the circular rim gives a water pressure below atmospheric by approximately Δp = 2γ cosθ / d. This pressure deficit acts over the circular area A = πr^2 and pulls the lower hemisphere upward with force F = Δp A. Compute the lower hemisphere weight from V = (2/3)πr^3 and W = ρ_g V g. Set F = W at the limiting separation, giving d = 3γ cosθ /(ρ_g g r), then insert r = 0.04 m, ρ_g = 19300 kg/m^3, γ = 0.072 N/m, θ = 10°, and convert meters to millimeters to get 0.0281 mm.

水的弯月面造成相对大气压的压力降低，近似为 Δp = 2γ cosθ / d。该压强差作用在圆面积 A = πr^2 上，给下半球向上的拉力 F = Δp A = (2γ cosθ / d)πr^2。

下半球体积为 V = (2/3)πr^3，因此重量 W = ρ_g V g = ρ_g (2/3)πr^3 g。

临界条件是向上的表面张力相关压力拉力等于下半球重量：
(2γ cosθ / d)πr^2 = ρ_g (2/3)πr^3 g。

约去公共因子后得到：
d = 3γ cosθ / (ρ_g g r)。

代入 r = 0.04 m，ρ_g = 19300 kg m^-3，γ = 0.072 N m^-1，θ = 10°，g = 9.81 m s^-2：
d = 3(0.072)cos(10°) / [19300(9.81)(0.04)] ≈ 2.81 × 10^-5 m。

换算为毫米：2.81 × 10^-5 m = 0.0281 mm。

According to the specified method, approximate the opposite flat cut surfaces of the two hemispheres as parallel circular plates of radius r, with spacing d.

The meniscus of the water causes a pressure decrease relative to atmospheric pressure, approximated as Δp = 2γ cosθ / d. This pressure difference acts on the circular area A = πr^2, giving the lower hemisphere an upward pulling force F = Δp A = (2γ cosθ / d)πr^2.

The volume of the lower hemisphere is V = (2/3)πr^3, so the weight W = ρ_g V g = ρ_g (2/3)πr^3 g.

The critical condition is that the upward surface-tension-related pressure pulling force equals the weight of the lower hemisphere:
(2γ cosθ / d)πr^2 = ρ_g (2/3)πr^3 g.

After canceling common factors, this gives:
d = 3γ cosθ / (ρ_g g r).

Substitute r = 0.04 m, ρ_g = 19300 kg m^-3, γ = 0.072 N m^-1, θ = 10°, g = 9.81 m s^-2:
d = 3(0.072)cos(10°) / [19300(9.81)(0.04)] ≈ 2.81 × 10^-5 m.

Converted to millimeters: 2.81 × 10^-5 m = 0.0281 mm.
